rules.text: Every approach shows a valid signal (red, yellow or green) and a non-negative, finite queue.
The N/S and E/W directions are never both non-red (green or yellow) in the same second.
Before a direction turns green, the opposite direction has been red for at least all_red_seconds.
A green always ends in yellow, and every yellow lasts at least yellow_seconds before red.
No approach waits at red with vehicles queued for more than 200 seconds.

counterfactual.change: Removed the single detector_fail event (events: [] instead of E fail at t=203); same steps/seed/timings. With normal detection the controller cycles EW/NS and NS wait stays ~17s, no max_wait violation, proving the failure depends on the detector_fail + actuated max_green/recall interaction.

args.explanation: Shrunk actuated intersection with detector_fail E from t=203 (duration 159) starves NS. EW green starts at ~148 and is held continuously through step 346 (>190s, exceeding max_green_seconds=87) despite large NS queues. The failed E detector makes EW appear partly empty (E queue 0) but W still queued, so actuated gap-out logic never sees EW empty, and max_green / wait-recall logic fails to force a switch (likely treats failed detector as suppressing recall). NS waits grow from 58s at failure start to 200s at step 345 and 201s at step 346, violating max_wait. Removing the detector_fail restores normal cycling and no violation.
